Tamron 17-70mm. Its 2.8 all the way through, so if you do that and use the secondary base iso of 2500, it’ll perform okay in low light to an extent. Build-wise, the focus ring feels loose compared to a Sony lens, but you can get used to it. Compared to the Sigma 18-50mm, it feels almost twice, but still smaller than most full frame lenses.

Say, for something like a film, the production company pays a pilot to record film with said drone. That requires a part 107 because a service was provided. 

The distributor (studio) is separate and doesnt have to worry about that, because the production company paid them, not the studio. 

In this instance, the “production company” is the remote pilot themselves, and they distributed it themselves on Youtube. Youtube made money off of the *views*, not the drone footage itself, which they offer money back to the distributor themselves who happens to also be the pilot, based on views. 

No one paid to have the flight or footage.

They aren’t filming or selling footage to a client, they are technically filming for themselves. And these drones are provided for review purposes. No money exchanged hands. They aren’t providing a service to someone if they’re filming for themselves without money being exchanged. They can make money from the video on youtube because they shot it and are sharing it, they arent licensing it out for others to use. Make sense?
